questions.text: In a [latex]B^{+}[/latex] tree, if the search -key value is 8 bytes long, the block size is 512 bytes and the block pointer size is 2 bytes, then maximum order of the [latex]B^{+}[/latex] tree is _______________.
questions.solution:
A node of order p has p block pointers and p [latex]-[/latex] 1 keys:
[latex]2p+8(p-1)\le512\Rightarrow10p\le520\Rightarrow p=52[/latex]

Answer: 52

questions.text:
Two transactions [latex]T_1 \; and \; T_2[/latex] are given as:

[latex]T_{1}:r_{1} (X)w_{1}(X)r_{1}(Y)w_{1}(Y) [/latex]
[latex]T_{2}:r_{2}(Y)w_{2}(Y)r_{2}(Z)w_{2}(Z)[/latex]

where [latex]r_{i}(V)[/latex] denotes a read operation by transaction [latex]T_{i}[/latex] on a variable V and [latex]w_{i}(V)[/latex] denotes a write operations by transaction [latex]T_{i}[/latex] on a variable V. The total number of conflict serializable schedules that can be formed by [latex]T_1 \; and \; T_2[/latex] is _____________.
questions.solution:
T1 = a1 a2 a3 a4 (a3, a4 use Y), T2 = b1 b2 b3 b4 (b1, b2 use Y). The only conflicts are on Y, so a schedule is conflict serializable iff all of T1's Y operations come before T2's, or the other way round.
- T1 before T2 on Y: a4 before b1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] the serial schedule T1 T2: 1 way.
- T2 before T1 on Y: b2 before a3. Of all [latex]\binom84=70[/latex] interleavings, 17 have a3 before b2, so 53 qualify.

Total = 1 + 53 = 54

Answer: 54

questions.text:
Consider the following tables T1 and T2.

In table T1, P is the primary key and Q is the foreign key referencing R in table T2 with ondelete cascade and on-update cascade. In table T2, R is the primary key and S is the foreign key referencing P in table T1 on-delete set NULL and on-update cascade. In order to delete record (3,8) from table T1, the number of additional records that need to be deleted from table T1 is _____.
questions.solution:
Deleting (3, 8) from T1: T2's S references T1.P with ON DELETE SET NULL, so the T2 row (8, 3) just gets S = NULL. No T2 row is deleted, so nothing cascades back into T1.

Answer: 0

questions.text:
An ER model of a database consists of entity types A and B. These are connected by a
relationship R which does not have its own attribute. Under which one of the following
conditions, can the relational table for R be merged with that of A?
questions.solution:
If R is many-to-one from A to B and A participates totally, each A-tuple is related to exactly one B-tuple. So B's key can be stored as a column (foreign key) in A's table without NULLs or repeats.

Answer: Relationship R is many-to-one and the participation of A in R is total
